citations.description: Ticket comment: 'AC4: 20 consecutive runs of the file under CI's exact settings (-n 4 --dist loadgroup, --timeout=300), each on a fresh basetemp, with git fsck run over every remote.git the run produced. Result: 20/20 with 31 passed, zero test failures and zero corrupt remotes.' — no run id, CI link, or log artifact provided.

findings.criterion: AC4 — The affected file passes at least 20 consecutive runs under CI's settings (`-n 4 --dist loadgroup`), with the evidence recorded in a comment.
findings.detail: AC4 is classified as codebase-verifiable (no [operator-attested] tag). The ticket comment asserts '20/20 with 31 passed, zero test failures and zero corrupt remotes' but provides no verifiable reference id, change URL, CI run link, or log artifact — only a bare assertion of outcome. A codebase-verifiable criterion cannot be satisfied by a ticket comment alone, and the repository itself cannot demonstrate 20 consecutive CI run results.
findings.remediation: Tag AC4 as [operator-attested] and record a concrete attestation in a ticket comment naming the specific CI run URL(s) or job id(s), the observed pass counts, and the date/timestamp of the 20-run sweep.

citations.description: Ticket comment: 'AC5: make lint and make typecheck pass; the full file passes (31 passed), as does the reconciler unit tree (2409 passed).' — no run id or log artifact provided.

findings.detail: AC5 is classified as codebase-verifiable (no [operator-attested] tag). The ticket comment states 'make lint and make typecheck pass' but provides no CI run id, Gerrit change verification link, or log artifact. A codebase-verifiable criterion cannot be satisfied by a bare assertion in a ticket comment.
findings.remediation: Tag AC5 as [operator-attested] and record a concrete attestation naming the specific CI run URL or Gerrit change id (e.g., change 1676) with Verified +1 status, the observed outcome, and when it was confirmed.

data.remediation: How to resolve the unmet criteria: use the evidence path that matches each one. For codebase-verifiable work, complete any unfinished work and make its proof discoverable in the repository. For evidence that inherently lives outside the repository, mark the criterion with the exact `[operator-attested]` tag and add a comment to this ticket that documents the concrete artifacts that meet it (commands and their output, links, or the reasoning that ties the evidence to the criterion). The completion verifier reads this ticket's comments, so properly tagged evidence you record there is taken into account on the next verification. An untagged external criterion cannot be satisfied by a ticket comment alone. Then re-verify.
